lessons.culture: The adhan calls to each of the five daily prayers, and in Iraq a masjid is usually called a "جامع". The iqamah comes a little later and means everyone stands in rows. Men and women usually use separate doors, and someone who arrives late joins the imam and completes the missed rak'ah after the salaam.

lessons.culture: Wudu comes before prayer, so a jami3 has a wudu area, usually near the restrooms. Shoes come off at the entrance and go on the rack, clothes should be clean, and phones go on silent. The qibla is the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah, and a niche called the محراب often marks it.

exercises.tip: "اكو" means "there is" and "ماكو" means "there isn't".

lessons.culture: On Friday the Jumu'ah prayer takes the place of Dhuhr and is prayed in congregation after the khutbah. People bathe, wear clean clothes and come early, and during the khutbah everyone listens in silence, since even whispering to a neighbour is discouraged. After the prayer people greet each other with "جُمُعَةٌ مُبَارَكَة"; in Iraq Friday is a day off for most people.

lessons.culture: Many jawami3 run Qur'an circles (حلقات) for adults and children, often after Maghrib or Fajr, where each student recites from memory to the teacher, who is called "أستاذ" or "شيخ". The mushaf is handled with clean hands, kept off the floor and returned to its shelf.

challenge.title: A Visit to the Jami3
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines at the masjid: ask about the next prayer and the iqamah, find the wudu area and the shoe rack, ask about the qibla, put your phone on silent, and say you missed a rak'ah. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 17.
required_elements: A question about the next prayer or the iqamah, using شنو or شوگت.
A question about the wudu area or an entrance, using وين.
A request for the shoe rack, a prayer rug or the qibla, or an order using حطّ.
A polite request about the phone using لو سمحت, answered with حاضر.
A missed rak'ah explained with فاتتني.
The fixed closing تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ with its reply مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ.
